newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to up, HSFO again gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to up, HSFO again gains.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were steady to up Monday in thin trade, with firm bunkers again boosting some high sulphur grades despite some weakness in crude, industry sources said.
"Bunkers are still pretty strong, so there's a little upward pressure on high sulphur," said one cash trader, noting low sulphur was steady but stifled by lack of demand.
In New York Harbor, high sulphurs gained 25 to 35 cents a barrel, with 2.2 percent now talked at $17.50-75 and three percent in the low-$17s, traders said.
NYH physical one percent held relatively steady at $19.00, with Oct paper quoted steady early at $19.35-65 but likely lower later with crude.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally was still offered at about $21, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was unchanged at about $17.50, while three percent notionally climbed 25-50 cents to about $17. No NYH or USG deals were reported.
October New York city gate gas was quoted little changed Monday at near the $2.20/mmBtu level versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.02/mmBtu equivalent.
